q: From 1 August 2023, e-invoicing applies to businesses whose aggregate turnover in any preceding FY (from 2017-18) exceeds:
exp: The threshold came down in phases from ₹500 crore to ₹5 crore.

q: Which documents need e-invoicing (IRN) for an applicable taxpayer?
options: B2B invoices, credit notes and debit notes, exports, and supplies to SEZ
exp: B2C invoices don't need an IRN. Very large taxpayers need a dynamic QR code on B2C invoices instead.

q: Which entity is exempt from e-invoicing regardless of turnover?
exp: Others exempt: insurers, GTAs, passenger transport, multiplex admissions, SEZ units, and government departments and local authorities.

q: Once a business crosses the e-invoice threshold in any year, it must continue e-invoicing even if turnover later falls below it.
exp: The test is 'any preceding FY from 2017-18'.

q: A company exceeding the threshold issues a B2B invoice without generating an IRN. What's the legal consequence?
options: The invoice isn't considered a valid tax invoice
exp: Rule 48(5). The buyer's ITC is also at risk, and penalties can apply.

q: What does IRN stand for?
exp: The Invoice Reference Number is a unique hash for the document.

q: The IRN is a 64-character hash generated using which algorithm?
exp: It's computed over the supplier's GSTIN, financial year, document type and document number.

q: Which fields generate the IRN hash?
options: Supplier GSTIN, buyer GSTIN, invoice value
Supplier GSTIN, financial year, document type, document number
exp: That's why the same document number can't be reused in the same FY for the same document type.

q: Who generates the IRN?
options: The IRP (Invoice Registration Portal), though the taxpayer can pre-compute it
exp: The IRP validates the invoice, generates or validates the IRN, and digitally signs the invoice and QR code.

q: Which of these is NOT in the signed QR code of an e-invoice?
exp: The QR also includes number of line items, IRN and IRN date.

q: In e-invoicing, the government generates the invoice for the taxpayer.
exp: The taxpayer creates the invoice in its own system. The IRP only registers, validates and signs it.

q: In the e-invoice JSON schema, what does supply type 'SEZWOP' mean?
options: Supply to SEZ without payment of tax (under LUT)
exp: Other values: B2B, SEZWP (with payment), EXPWP, EXPWOP, DEXP (deemed export).

q: For an export invoice in the e-invoice schema, what's entered as the buyer's GSTIN?
exp: For exports, the buyer GSTIN is 'URP', place of supply state code 96, and pincode 999999.

q: What's state code 96 used for in e-invoices?
exp: 97 is Other Territory. 96 marks a destination outside India.

q: What's the 'IgstOnIntra' flag in the e-invoice schema for?
options: Cases where IGST applies even though supplier and POS are in the same state, like SEZ supplies
exp: Without it, validation expects CGST+SGST when supplier state equals POS.

q: Minimum HSN digits required on e-invoices for businesses with AATO above ₹5 crore:
exp: Those at or below ₹5 crore need 4 digits for B2B.

q: Within how long can an e-invoice (IRN) be cancelled on the IRP?
exp: After 24 hours, you have to cancel it manually in GSTR-1 before filing, or issue a credit note.

q: Partial cancellation of an e-invoice is allowed on the IRP.
exp: Only full cancellation. To change something, cancel it and issue a new one with a different number, or use a credit or debit note.

q: After cancelling an IRN, you can generate a new IRN using the same invoice number.
exp: The number is locked once used, since the hash would be identical. Use a new document number.

q: From 1 April 2025, taxpayers with AATO of ₹10 crore or more can't report e-invoices to the IRP older than:
exp: This time limit earlier applied only to AATO ≥ ₹100 crore, from November 2023.

q: Can an e-invoice be amended on the IRP?
options: No, amendments aren't allowed on the IRP; changes are made through GSTR-1 amendment or credit/debit notes
exp: This is why validation before submission matters.

q: After the IRP registers an e-invoice, where does the data flow automatically?
options: To GSTN (auto-populating the supplier's GSTR-1 and buyer's GSTR-2B) and to the e-way bill system if transport details are given
Only to the income tax department
exp: This is the core efficiency gain of e-invoicing.

q: Can an e-way bill be generated along with the IRN?
options: Yes, if transport details (Part B or transporter ID) are included in the e-invoice request
exp: The IRP passes the data to the e-way bill system.

q: There are multiple IRPs, including the NIC-run IRP and several private IRPs authorised by GSTN.
exp: Taxpayers can choose any IRP; they all feed the same GST system.

q: A client's ERP generates an e-invoice but the IRP rejects it with a duplicate IRN error. The client says the invoice was never registered. What are the likely causes and how would you debug?
model: A duplicate IRN error means an IRN already exists for the same supplier GSTIN, financial year, document type and document number. Likely causes: a previous request did succeed but the response was lost (timeout or network error) so the ERP didn't store it; someone generated it through another IRP or the portal; or the same number was used earlier in the FY. Debug by calling the get-IRN-by-document-details API to fetch the existing IRN, then store and print it. If it was cancelled earlier, the number can't be reused, so issue a new number. Also make IRN requests idempotent by checking before retrying.
points: Duplicate = same GSTIN + FY + doc type + doc number
Lost response after a successful call
exp: Timeout handling is one of the most common real-world e-invoice bugs.

q: A client generated an e-invoice with the wrong buyer GSTIN two days ago. What's the fix?
options: It's past 24 hours, so issue a credit note for the full value and a fresh e-invoice with a new number to the correct buyer
exp: After the 24-hour window the IRN can't be cancelled on the IRP.

q: A client's turnover was ₹6 crore in FY 2022-23 but only ₹4 crore since. It stopped generating IRNs. Is that okay?
options: No, crossing the threshold in any year from 2017-18 keeps e-invoicing mandatory
exp: The test is 'any preceding financial year'.

q: A client's ERP was down on the 28th, so a salesperson issued a handwritten B2B invoice without an IRN. What's the problem?
options: For an e-invoice-applicable client, an invoice without IRN isn't a valid tax invoice; generate the e-invoice on the IRP (within the reporting time limit) before goods go
exp: The buyer's ITC depends on it, and e-way bill checks can flag goods moving without an IRN.

q: The IRP rejects an e-invoice because the buyer's GSTIN is 'cancelled'. The client insists the buyer is active. What's the check?
options: Search the GSTIN on the portal to confirm status and effective date; if cancelled, the sale should be treated as B2C
exp: IRPs validate GSTIN status against GSTN master data.
